title: Film scene score: scene-based background music, what it must and must not do

structure.cue_in_out: from the spotting notes: the director's start and end timecodes and a mood for each cue
structure.hit_points: only the moments that matter; the strongest land on a downbeat
structure.diegetic_vs_score: source music that the characters hear is placed in the room (reverb, level and EQ of the space); a score is heard only by the audience

dialogue_underscore.register: very low or high; keep the 1-5 kHz band light
dialogue_underscore.why: dense midrange scoring under dialogue competes with the voice; the lower strings sit where the voice sits

suspense.register: low drones, high tremolo, a pulse
suspense.why: tension from a held or pulsing bed, not from a melody

action.why: drive and size; hits land on the picture; the dialogue and effects still own the centre

emotional.register: mid, a single line or a small group
emotional.why: a simple line the picture can carry, not a mood the picture already shows

montage.why: no dialogue, so the music can carry the passage of time

source_music.register: as the source, placed in the room
source_music.why: music the characters hear is part of the scene and sits at the room's level, then ducks under speech

transition.why: carry the listener across a cut without announcing it

silence.why: when a scene needs nothing beyond what the picture and sound show, no music is the right cue

mixing.two_versions: a full version for where there is no dialogue and an underscore version for where there is; cut between them
mixing.bed_vs_program_lufs: the cue is a bed under a dialogue-gated program (references/data/presets/film/delivery.json); judge it against the dialogue, not alone
techniques: EQ the music, not only duck it: take 2-4 dB out of 2.5-5 kHz while the voice is there
keep the low end tight and the top crisp, with the midrange reduced
sparse instrumentation: a high bell with a low plucked bass instead of a full string quartet under speech
audition the music with the real dialogue and effects, never soloed
fade out of silence and into it on purpose; a cue that begins and ends on a hit is a decision

dos.text: Decide where each cue starts and ends, and its mood, from the spotting notes before writing.
Hit the few moments that matter, ideally on a downbeat, and set the tempo so the hits land.
Keep the midrange light under dialogue and take 2-4 dB out of 2.5-5 kHz while a voice is speaking.
Choose sparse instrumentation under dialogue: a high and a low voice rather than a full middle.
Check the music against the real dialogue and effects, not soloed.
Give a recurring character, place or idea a short theme that can change as the story does.
Put music a character hears in the room: its level, reverb and EQ come from the space, and it is non-diegetic only when it leaves the room.
Leave a scene without music when it needs nothing beyond what the picture already shows.

donts.text: Do not hit everything you see: that is mickey-mousing and reads as cartoon in live action; drama needs fewer hits.
Do not put a lush, midrange-heavy score where the voice is (about 1-5 kHz).
Do not run the full-arrangement version of a cue under dialogue.
Do not judge the music in isolation; a mix that sounds a range short alone is often right in the film.
Do not score the emotion the picture and the acting already carry.
Do not let a temp track decide the cue: directors can attach to it, so take its function and mood, not its notes.
Do not drop a stock cue in place of a scored one: music that does not follow the scene reads as clip art.
Do not start or end a cue where nothing changes: there are no fixed rules, but each in and out is a decision the spotting notes record.

provenance.structure.cue_in_out: spotting sessions: start and end timecodes and a mood description per cue (Packt, Berklee Online, B&H Explora)
provenance.structure.hit_points: hit points are moments the music should synchronise with; the most effective land on a downbeat (Packt, Art of Composing)
provenance.structure.hits_per_minute_max_for_drama: starting value: the sources say a drama should not hit everything, and give no figure
provenance.structure.diegetic_vs_score: definitions in the sources of knowledgebase/media/film-scene-score-dos-and-donts.md section 3
provenance.scenes: starting values for energy, density and duck depth (no sourced figures were found); the family choices follow the practitioner advice quoted in the knowledge file
provenance.mixing.speech_band_hz: practitioner ranges disagree: about 1-3 kHz (MusicTech), 1-5 kHz (a studio blog), 2.5-5 kHz (ProSoundWeb)
provenance.mixing.intelligibility_band_hz: ProSoundWeb: the band that most affects speech intelligibility is 2.5-5 kHz
provenance.mixing.carve_cut_db: ProSoundWeb: reduce the music 2-4 dB in that band while boosting the voice there
provenance.mixing.techniques: ProSoundWeb, MusicTech, c-istudios and Robin Hoffmann as quoted in the knowledge file; practitioner advice
